accessibility: The page has one level-1 heading ("Overview"); the attention items are real buttons with their full text as the accessible name and 44px touch targets on tablet and phone; the headline is a status region.
Table headers are visible on desktop and tablet; on phones each card repeats the field labels so meaning never depends on column position.
Readiness and evidence states pair color with an icon and a word; the updated dot carries its words for assistive technology.
No text renders below 12px in any Locale; controls use 13px and prose 14px, and zh-TW line heights grow by about 2px.
Light and dark themes meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast for text and controls.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Rail, NavItem, Button, Stack, Text, Badge, Icon, Skeleton, SegmentedControl, Segment, TextInput, TabBar and TabBarItem); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.
The Overview never edits canonical resources; export and navigation are its only actions.
Green appears only for success (Clean, Ready); blocked readiness uses fault red with an icon and a count.

The filters are buttons: the Adapter has no Select that opens inline in the table filters; the real page has two selects (feature, shown with more than one feature, and readiness) and sortable column headers.

The sidebar shows the three primary destinations, the Workspace entry and the collapse button, as the real one does; the Workspace pages (Settings, Locales, Assets, Product Kit) are reached from the Workspace entry and are not repeated here. The navbar is the real one: Workspace mark, location, search, member and preferences.

Every visible string is bound with $i18n. en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets; zh-TW uses Taiwan Traditional Chinese with full-width punctuation and keeps domain nouns (View, Variant, Widget, Workspace, Review, Spec, UX Flow, Handoff, Adapter, Locale, Asset, Decision, Owner, Checks, Evidence) in English.

Identities and measurements stay literal and use the mono blueprint register: feature tags, Widget ids and type names, revisions, keyboard keys and CLI commands are never translated. The sample Views and their counts are sample content.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A signed-in member opened the Workbench root or chose Overview in the sidebar, the tablet icon rail or the phone bottom bar. A Workspace with no View shows the first-run steps instead of the tabs (Overview: first run).
Readiness is computed by the same assessment as assess_handoff_readiness; the page only presents it.

The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset (desktop 1920 × 1080, tablet 1024 × 768, or mobile 390 × 844), one Locale (en-US default or zh-TW), and one theme (light or dark). All twelve combinations are authored and captured explicitly.
spec.intent: Answer "what needs me, and what is ready to hand off?" at a glance: an attention headline, then every View with its Reviews, Checks, Evidence and Handoff readiness, so an Owner can export implementation-ready work and unblock the rest. This is the Views tab, the default of the five Overview tabs.
interactionRules: The headline lists what needs attention as display-size buttons: waiting for review, open threads, and blocked Views; zero counts are left out. Each one navigates to the matching list; with nothing waiting it reads "Nothing waiting" with the number of Views that are ready, and with a Workspace schema this UIUX does not support it says that Reviews and readiness are unavailable.

The tabs are Views, Checks, Decisions, Requirements (only with a requirement source of the spec kind) and Activity; the tab in effect is the address, and switching it adds no history entry. The Views tab shows a sortable table: View, Feature, Reviews, Checks, Evidence and Readiness, filterable by name, feature and readiness.

Readiness reads "Ready" only when the closure has fresh complete Evidence, no open or ready-for-review Review threads and no blocking diagnostics; otherwise it names the number of blocking issues. A View whose readiness is being read says "Checking…", one that could not be read says "Couldn't check", and an unsupported Workspace says "Can't check".
Evidence shows fresh and stale capture counts, "None" without any capture and "Unknown" when freshness cannot be judged; stale means the View, Locale or render-context preset changed since capture.

A View changed since this browser last looked carries a dot with the words "Updated since you last looked", and the View opened last is marked "Last opened". A row opens the View on its Readiness tab.
"Export handoff…" opens the Handoff export for the selected roots; it is offered to a member with the export key on tablet and desktop.

Layout derives from the viewport width only: 1280px and wider shows the 264px sidebar, the main region and (where present) a 340px right panel; 768–1279px collapses the sidebar to a 56px icon rail; below 768px the sidebar is replaced by the 56px bottom TabBar. On phones each table row becomes an outlined card with labelled fields.
